reviews.text: You might be able to guess from my playtime, but I recommend Die in the Dungeon and believe it has a long replayability. [b]Theme[/b] The frogs as main characters and little insects and bugs are such a cool theme - games don't do this enough. The art and animation really shine and make this game stand out. The world-building is consistent and helps the eclectic nature of the theme really mesh. This original theme is really what drew me in. [b]Strategy[/b] You would think a game about rolling digital dice would be heavily luck focused, but instead, strategy takes the center stage. This game has crazy player agency and strong meta synergies between systems. And this is because the game is _unique_ - It's not a traditional deckbuilder like slay the spire, or a dice based roguelike or rpg like maybe slice and dice (both great games btw) Die in the Dungeon has the board, where dice directly interact with each other: - boost dice affect dice placement and value of the action dice - terrain dice allow you to stack value directly on the board for future turns (further influencing dice placement) - flash property allows dice to transcend the board limitations, but give up some placement benefits - mirror and prism and such are all about manipulating spacing of dice THIS is what sets DitD apart - it's more than draw, dice rolling, and energy cost. The placement and board system is much deeper and is the driver for crazy deck synergy. (side-note: many of the enemies also interact with the board directly. This is what gives enemies variety, even when their "actions" might just be attack or block for the most part) [b]Deck Crafter[/b] Last point just said the game wasn't really a deck builder lol. But I really want to point out how much player agency the player has when crafting their deck. - face value manipulation: not just upgrading for higher faces, but directly controlling the value the die rolls. This system is supported by various relics, the board shape for placement, and general value/consistency tradeoffs - Properties: you can add two properties to each die, that can radically change how they are played - Unique/niche dice: Things like mirror variants, prism, new thorns (it got a rework recently), new generator, new puncture (also reworked recently), new multiplier, hollower, fortify... AND these dice can sometimes come as "mixed" dice which have the abilities of two different dice. - relics: the fact is, the game has over 100 relics. There is a lot of variety and synergy between relics and your dice, and some relics are incredibly build altering. [b]Replay Value[/b] If you haven't seen half the points listed above, then that is proof of the replay value. Some dice types, relics, etc. are unlocked with various achievements or by leveling up the frogs. I mean this respectfully, but there is no possible way to see all the game has to offer after just 4 runs. - 4 different frogs with 2 starter relics apiece that encourage very different strategies - 8 levels of difficulty if you like "ascensions" - endless mode with a focus on battles and power scaling - 59 achievements (with in-game unlocks) And if you run out of things to do in the game: - speedrunning - challenges (no heal, starter dice only, no relics, no attack...) - leveling up all the frogs - insane builds [b]Dev Team & Community[/b] Final point goes to the dev team. This is a brother duo behind the game that was first created in a game jam. This is an indie game and a labor of love. Furthermore, the devs have very much made the community part of the creation process. Not just content creators or testers - they have implemented lots of feedback and suggestions from players that have made the game better. [b]Fair Criticisms[/b] I think these are fair to point out, but don't pose so much of a concern to keep me from recommending the game: - Polish: This is an indie game, so you don't get AAA polish. There is the occasional visual glitch, UI issue, or controller goof. The devs patch these very quickly if you report the issue (in-game feedback even, no discord or google form required). There's also some performance issues if you restart a run several times. But the game still feels very fun to play. And some tutorials and tooltips could be more helpful if you don't like just trying out that new die or relic to see what it does - RnG: I think this is a fair criticism too. Some of the reward pools (especially relics and dice) feel a little weird, and not quite truly random or generated. I am NOT talking about RnG on dice draws and rolls. Sometimes it feels bad to not get the die or roll you wanted, but the game gives plenty of player agency in deck crafting. - Difficulty: some things are a bit "overtuned" and it is hard for me to see this now due to the amount of hours I have in the game. But the first run, and D0 difficulty in general are specifically presented in a way to make the game accessible to new players, but this can get old after a couple runs. The difficulty can spike between areas and difficulty levels in ways that require some "meta" knowledge (strategy) to overcome. Again, I still recommend the game. Try it for yourself. If you end up having any of these concerns, I think it is valid, but I don't think this will end up spoiling your enjoyment either. At current price, I think the game is a steal. Of course, I'm hoping for post-launch content updates beyond just fixes, but if the dev team hops into a new project instead, I'll jump on board that too.

游戏机制是挺有意思的，但这次抢先体验版比前几次demo的难度也高太多了， 1.d1怪物的数值比d0感觉至少提升了50%，除非有非常好的遗物搭配，否则根本不可能打过，都不敢想后面的d2-d4会有多难。 2.问号房90%都是战斗，极大降低了不确定性带来的良好体验。 3.金币前期给太少，到达第一个商店前经常买不起任何一个遗物。 4.大部分遗物的数值实在太低，需要苛刻条件才能触发的每回合两三点的伤害或者一两点的数值加成在连小怪都几十血，10+攻的面板下根本没有任何用。 5.部分小怪太超模，随便单拎出来比boss都强，例如第一层的模仿怪+不受到攻击攻击次数就会+1的怪的组合。第二层的每回合10+伤害，30左右的血并且不精准击杀就会无限复活的怪。第三层单独作为小怪的蜜蜂，本身不大的棋盘被强行占据一个格子的同时还会有多个格子数值被直接减半。 我相信这个游戏如果数值重新设计一下应该会大幅改善体验，至少在前几次demo的时候，我玩着还是很有乐趣的，先给好评观望下吧。

Before I get to the harsh details of this review, I will admit it - the game has interesting & different mechanics, I have not seen in other rogue-like games. Bosses also feel super unique and playing around them feels very rewarding. And so are the regular enemies in the game - they are quite charming and the art direction is superb. I mean what's not to love playing as a cute frog and throw unique dice on the board? But rIght now... I'd say only play this if you're on the hunt for more dice deckbuilding rogue-likes, such as SpellRogue, Slice and Dice, Astrea. And this is coming from someone who was very much looking forward to playing Die in the Dungeon after testing out both origins and the latest demo. Thing is - while the music and whole feel of the world is fantastic, this early access is just not that great, tbh. So I want to share the feedback with the devs after completing 2 runs (1 loss, 1 win). List of issues (at least to me personally) as of now: - Tooltips are NOT shown in a lot of menus ( e.g. while in the map, you CANNOT review properties of dice inside the bag...). If I have to make a choice for my dice, I need to always know what those properties are doing, I don't have a perfect memory. - Information is not always fully disclosed. E.g. Regen dice, it says it will restore HP every turn and then decrease. What it doesn't tell you, it always gets reduced by HALF so from Regen 8 you drop to 4 next turn. - Dice drafting after beating normal enemies is NOT exciting enough. Seriously, both my runs had very few dice because most dice offered either have crappy properties OR they are just basic versions. The most exciting dice usually come from the Act bosses but I'd wish at least Elite fights offered cool dice too. - Run time is suuuuuper long. Maybe I am stupid and need time to think but jesus, both runs ended up lasting about 2h 50m (and I lost the first run because of normal enemies dogpiling me after unlucky dice pull in end of Act 3) - Horrible, HORRIBLE optimization issues. I thought it was my PC but I saw other people on the forums saying the same thing - this game loads sometimes up to 5-8 seconds for screen transitions, when you hover over tooltips, the game stutters or lags and so on. - Variety of relics offered during the run feel kinda samey - maybe it's just the first 2 runs ... but both times I ended up with almost identical relics, I can't recall how many rogue-like games in early access had this same issue but it felt like my runs only mattered in terms of picking different dice. - The dice board itself - white innovative, definitely needs some visual clarity on multiple statuses stacking on top of 1 space. For example, Voltage or Honey stacking with spaces that already had other statuses, one of them overrides it visually and you have to hover over that space to see what exactly is happening inside it. - The map traversal, while functional is... boring. We've seen this same thing in many roguelikes, I remember the devs in the demo made a peculiar traversal board where you use dice to move, like roll & move board game, which admittedly was very swingy and random but at least it felt different. Maybe you can work on the map traversal and introduce some unique, dice-themed ways to play around it? - Elite rooms are super boring. It's just 2 waves of regular enemies you can see anywhere else. I'd really wish these rooms contained unique enemies you won't see in regular fights. (as in most rogue-likes) That's most of the stuff off the top of my head, I won't review the balance of the game because... I've only played it twice but I didn't notice massive balancing issues. Maybe the ramp up of raw stats for enemies in act 2 and 3 is a bit too much and makes some dice properties near useless. Like the one that poisons for 2... on an enemy that has 70+ HP in act 3 this just feels like a wasted slot on a dice. Anyway, I don't want to sound too negative, overall this game has very strong potential. But I was quite surprised after waiting so long for it, it definitely feels very half-baked at the moment, I understand it's the early access but c'mon... these days devs use EA as an excuse to get funding for the development, which is totally fine but if we're playing by these rules, then it'd be great to wait for the game to be polished enough to be enjoyable without all the extra content that's supposedly coming in the future. I only say "supposedly" because after buying so many indie rogue-likes, most of them are abandoned when they don't make enough money.

目前玩了将近10个小时，通关了4次，一局大概一个半小时。这个游戏骰子和棋盘格的玩法在爬塔肉鸽里面还是很新颖的，boss战也挺有设计的。美术和音乐也很不错。 以下是我个人游玩中，发现的一些问题。 1.在后期数值膨胀很快，特别是第三张地图（d1难度小怪就99血十几点伤害），多个小怪开局攻击就是几十点，人物也就那么多血，如果鬼抽（首牌稀烂）了，没拿到一张防御，攻击也打不死敌人，基本上就暴毙了。希望可以加入类似于杀戮尖塔药水的东西，增加一些容错。 2.感觉问号房遇敌概率有些高，点进去经常都是触发战斗，问号房的事件目前版本也比较少。 3.精英战斗可以设计一些精英怪，而不是两波小兵。 4.非战斗房（商店，铁匠，篝火，删骰子，事件）种类比较多，感觉篝火和删骰子可以整合在一起。 5.这游戏遗物非常重要，拿到好的遗物组合，基本上可以乱杀，骰子的数值也上来了。目前版本的遗物对于肉鸽游戏来说还是不够多，一局内经常遇到很多重复遗物。 6.并不是骰子越多越好，拿到关键的骰子，给骰子上关键的属性很重要（比如同类，空心）。每场战斗结束可以三选一一个骰子但是大部分都没什么用一般都是跳过。 7.第二章那个需要精准击杀的小怪很烦......没有精准击杀被打死了还会攻击你，如果数值过高或者是过低没有精准击杀，需要干掉三次才能打败这个小怪。
可爱蛙蛙，地牢厮杀， 狗屎骰子，把我摩擦， 数值失衡，伤害刮痧， D2坐牢，策划死妈！

I want to recommend this but, right now, it just feels more frustrating than rewarding. I wanted to give it a really solid chance because of how much I liked Origins but getting to the third stage over and over and then not getting any new unlocks or anything on dying more often than not, and one wrong move, even just having not max health, basically means you should just give up the run at the third stage point... yeah. I just feel frustrated and not in a good way. Between that and the dice you get rarely seeming worth much. It just felt too luck based and then also punishing. I know its Early Access so I hope at some point I can change my review. Though, right now, it's just not for me. And, for the record so you know where I'm coming from, I have played a lot of games like Slay the Spire and roguelikes in general and do decent at them and don't get this feeling I get with this of 'oh no, not another enemy I have to kill by exact count' as though it's some chore and not just a challenge and so on. Though, again, there's so much about the core mechanics I like that I hope this problem just gets ironed out or, maybe, this is just for people who want punishing and zero margin for error in luck or tactics.

很遗憾，虽然这款游戏，画面可爱，玩法新颖有趣，可是制作组糟糕的数值把控使得我无法给它打好评。 一方面，游戏内对骰子本身的数值给得极为克制，需要在铁匠铺提升点数，又加了骰子等级来限制这个加点，可是在另一方面，又有着镜像骰子这个能直接翻倍的骰子，可以将数字极大提升，使得一次游玩顺不顺利，很大程度上看拿到镜像骰子早不早，骰子词条好不好。也许是受此影响，敌人的数值也十分别扭，用了镜像能轻松应对，不用的话，最好的情况也是刮痧一万年，尤其本游戏敌人种类较少，精英关要打的只是更多的小怪，更是加重了游玩时的疲惫感。 镜像对平衡的破坏远不止如此，像是吃不到镜像的迅捷骰子，直接成了下水道，词条的中毒玩起来也是无比鸡肋。不同流派的平衡完全被破坏了，如果这个游戏真的有能称得上流派的构筑的话。 在高难度下，数值的问题愈发凸显，由于铁匠没有了免费升级，骰子的数值难以调整，进而导致大量遗物不能触发，战斗更加艰难，更加漫长枯燥，形成恶性循环，游玩体验直线下降。 与此同时，由于所有角色公用卡池，角色技能存在感又低（高的那个已经被削了），不同角色区分度低，构筑的重点：骰子，其点数和词条的调整又被稀少的资源紧紧卡着，导致难以组出差异大的构筑，游戏趣味大大减少，此情况在高难度下尤甚。 于是，糟糕的数值，漫长乏味的战斗，难以成型的构筑，崩坏的平衡，这几点共同将游戏导向了一个可怕的结果——无聊、枯燥。这个缺点足以将它其他优点全部改过去。 总而言之，很遗憾的游戏，至少现在，我不推荐

I loved the game when it was a demo version and I happily got it as an EA version, but I cannot recomend it to anyone who gets motion sickness in games or has motion-sensitive migraines. The devs added too many passive, rhythmic, aggressively looping animations that you can't turn off. The character? Wiggles. The enemies? Wiggle. The cursor? Wiggles. The stats? Wiggle. The background? Yeah, it is also animated. Gave me a migraine in about 15 minutes. The devs don't seem to have any accesibility features planned from what I have seen; I have noticed that the request on discord for accessibility mode (not by me) has been archived, which makes me think they decided against it. If I wasn't past the refund period, I would've applied for one. Overall: promnising game but if you have any sensetivity issues at all, move along. ETA: as the full version of the game is out, I went in to check if anything changed. As far as I see, everything stayed the same. I understand a small team might have no resources to add something like accessibility mode, but as it stands, I cannot look at the battle screen for more than 2 minutes. It's not even the fact that things move, but the fact that all the movement is rhythmic, repetative, and out of sync rhythmically from other on-screen elements.

Die in the Dungeon is missing somethings that make it feel off. Objectively, its a good game, but when other Roguelikes just fill me with endless replayable joy, and I simply don't want to bother with Die any longer than I have to, I can't really give it a positive score. I like that the battles are fast paced, I like that after just one run most players will be able to tell that certain types of dice and certain types of dice powers are traps. The art style is by far the best part of the game. I also really like that your starting equipment and dice are, for the most part, actually worth keeping the entire run, which is not true for other roguelikes like slay the spire and its hundred clones. But its missing something. There isn't exactly a lot of plot. There are codex entries for characters and enemies, but that doesn't really build a world, despite the evocative names for the three acts. I didn't like that I unlocked endless mode on my 2nd run, and the implication that endless was the seemingly most important way to play. I don't like that there seems to be only one viable strategy with bare variations on it. I don't like that rejecting all your offered dice each reward pick is genuinely the superior choice every single time. I don't like that the artifacts are weak and rarely encourage you to build powerful archetypical decks. The payoffs aren't there. what is my reward for filling my dice bag with glass? with gold? Hollow? Pack? Poison seems like a strategy that would power up in multiples, but the chance of getting more than 2 poison upgrades in a single run seems impossible. Growth is legitimately insane and if your dice back is small enough a single grow dice can win a run all by itself. There aren't enough different map events, vendors, or types of choices. The number of times I'd open up the map and be presented with the same exact choices for the next 5 nodes, and 3 different but identical paths that all converge after that point, just seemed, to be frank, silly and undercooked. The mechanics aren't here. I've beaten four runs so far, over two separate characters, and I just don't feel any need to play the game anymore. The game is highly, highly polished, but It genuinely feels like ive seen everything the game has to offer, and grinding out exp for codex entries and even more mediocre artifacts does not seem worth my time. It doesn't do what I need a roguelike to actually do.

[h1][b]青蛙闯地牢，骰子本领高[/b][/h1] 纵观茫茫多的肉鸽游戏，我们总能发现骰子的身影，这枚小小的骰子正好符合了肉鸽游戏的特点，既有一定的随机性，又在可控范围内，加上构筑元素便带来了绝佳的策略性。 《骰死地牢（Die in the Dungeon）》便是一款以骰子管理为主要玩法的肉鸽作品，游戏中玩家将扮演可爱的小青蛙进入地牢冒险，用骰子、遗物、药水等搭配击溃一切拦路的敌人。 游戏的底层框架是大家熟悉的《杀戮尖塔》这套，拥有抽牌、弃牌、能量值、怪物意图等机制。 骰子拥有不同的类型，比如攻击、格挡、治疗、强化等，前面几个很容易理解，强化骰子会在放置时强化附近的槽位，放置在该槽位的骰子便会得到数值增强。 战斗界面的最中央是一个大大的骰子盘，玩家需要将抽到的骰子放入其中，利用骰子互相增强的特点最大化其效果，最终消灭敌人。 和我们熟知的一样，骰子由数个面组成，每个面都有不同的数字，每次抽取到时则会随机到一个面。 一般常规骰子的点数分配都是按阶梯式规律增长的，比如六面骰的112233，而一些作用强大的骰子，点数分配就兼具了风险设计，比如四面骰的0112等，抽到2皆大欢喜，抽到0就只能弃之不用了。 但其实还有各种不同的方法来补足这一点，本作打造了一个类似于爬塔的分支地图，上面同样拥有各种事件，比如战斗、商店、休息点、随机遭遇等，一路上管理骰子的机会有很多。 除了上述提到的强化外，便可以通过商店事件增加骰子的点数，比如将0112加到1223，或是重新分配点数，比如将0112改为1111，这样最差也能有一定的作用，当然了想要赌一把的话也可以选择提升上限。 本作的另一大特色是各种怪物机制，其会在玩家的骰子盘上做手脚，比如禁用槽位、弱化槽位等，此举为战斗增加了更多变数。 此外肉鸽游戏必不可少的遗物系统、药水系统，本作也没有落下，前者作用于全局，后者则可以提供强大的临时buff，这些内容的搭配同样也是玩法之一。 整体来说《骰死地牢》的这套玩法挺有意思，骰子盘的加入让数值的变化更加直观，使得玩家可以更好的规划战斗策略，骰子的管理则带来了无限可能。 此外游戏的画面表现也非常不错，还有多角色、无尽模式等内容可玩，目前游戏已更新到了正式版本，喜欢回合策略肉鸽的玩家可以一试。 [quote]热爱游戏，畅玩游戏，分享游戏，专注鉴赏评测与深度解析 欢迎关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44110339/]游理游据[/url]，走进游戏世界，品味第九艺术[/quote]

Where Slay The Spire has speed and fights that last between 1-10 turns, Die in the Dungeon feels slow and like a drag. Almost every build I've tried has ended up being a conservative sensible build where I don't lose any HP. The max health being so low (compared to StS with 70-80 max health) means that I'm being discouraged from trying new things. Where there are more rare dice with more abstract effects, they often seem to be too expensive to use, and are better to just ignore unless a very clear synergy is available. Most of the time, a successful run relies on finding a few overpowered relics. There is no punishment for a fight being 15+ turns, and often the enemies have very low damage and very high health, which contributes to a very slow, drawn out experience. I don't want my run to last 90 minutes when I feel like I can have the same experience in StS that's 30 minutes. As an experienced tactical roguelike player, there just seems to be so many out there that do it better than Die in the Dungeon.

[h2]前言[/h2] 《骰死地牢》是一款由ATICO制作HypeTrain Digital发行的肉鸽卡牌游戏。通常来说如果一个肉鸽是回合制，那么他烧脑程度绝对是呈指数上升，当然在这款游戏里也印证了这句话~ [h2]骰子能有多难啊，你别急让我算算！[/h2] 在这款游戏里，我们将扮演青蛙英雄勇闯地牢，在各种风格的怪物下杀出一条血路。但其实废话不用多说，3分钟理解剧情之后，其实就是通过各种骰子和遗物来构建自己想要的流派。游戏的流派非常多，每个角色本身也有其初始时不同的能力方便玩家更靠近对应流派，譬如LISVER就是标准毒流派代表。当然前期其实并不重要，最终还是看游玩过程中能获取哪些王炸遗物，并以此构建后续的流派内容。 当然游戏相比较别的肉鸽卡牌游戏最大的区别还是引用了骰子这个要素，如果简单理解那就是一个卡牌拥有最多8个不同的数值，在抽取时才能确定具体数值。举个例子当我有一个0224四面的攻击骰子，我抽到这个“卡牌”时还需要注意这个攻击骰子具体是4点攻击还是0点。那有的玩家就会问了，022这三个攻击不是纯纯debuff吗？ 显然不是的，因为有些遗物会有某些具体点数骰子的额外加成，甚至0点更能打出高额伤害。所以如此多的规则导致的就是构建流派的多样以及更需要玩家们深思熟虑去决策每一个细节。 此外游戏的棋盘也很有特色，菱形九格，需要玩家将骰子放上去算作生效。而由于一些特殊骰子有距离、buff这两个概念，就需要玩家合理的摆放骰子位置来获取最大输出。而诸如一些占格子的骰子(延迟流派，骰子在格子上持续生效)，那就得好好考虑什么时机放进去，不然很容易因为没有格子被怪物杀掉。 [h2]总结[/h2] 总的来说，在这些内容的加持下整体而言绝对称得上Rogue回合制牌组构建系列游戏的代表作之一。如果你喜欢这个类型游戏，还又被Mega Crit伤透了心，那不妨试试这款刚出正式版且还在打折的《骰死地牢》了~ [quote]关注「 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45108085/]游戏边界鉴赏组 [/url] 」[/quote] [u][b] “游戏边界”，一个打破游戏界限的地方 [/b][/u]

I really want to like this game. It's cute! I like roguelike deckbuilders. The dice matrix is neat. The four classes are all varied in interesting ways. But man, this game has some horrific problems. First and biggest, the dice matrix becomes unreadable if you ever have 2 effects on one space, which will happen constantly. Sometimes you'll have more than that. Some fights, especially the secret fight, are basically illegible. This slows down an already brutally slow game, making runs take well over an hour despite extremely simple decision making. And despite that extremely simple decision making, the "ascension" difficulties are brutal. Based on community feedback, it seems like the solution is to learn how to break the game over your knee with infinite combos. Can't go infinite? Sorry, simple value plays have no business here. Half the dice you're offered in act one actually make your deck worse. Half the relics do nothing, and the other half solve the game for you. I always feel like I'm either slowly sailing to victory or completely stonewalled, with no variance in between. High tier difficulty adds way, way to terrible of negative modifiers that again push you towards those infinite combos. Maybe you like solving games like a puzzle, and don't mind brutal difficulty, I don't, and regardless the illegibility and pace of this game are massive problems.

On paper this should be a dream game for fans of the genre. I’m a huge fan of roguelike deckbuilders, and “cards but with dice” plus dungeon crawling with a cute frog checked all the right boxes. The problem is that somewhere between the concept and the execution, they forgot to make it actually fun. The core issue is how unintuitive everything feels moment to moment. Every turn demands minute, fussy readings of dice descriptions, interactions, and edge cases just to understand what your options really are. Instead of that satisfying “I see my line, now I make a clever play” feeling you get in the best deckbuilders, you constantly stop to re‑read tooltips and decode the board. It’s more like doing homework on dice faces than making interesting decisions. Layer in the swingy low rolls and undertuned damage, and runs end up feeling punishing and opaque rather than challenging in a good way. When a game nails this genre, complexity becomes satisfying depth; here it too often feels like clutter getting between you and any actual fun.

If I could give it a 'meh' I would, but I can't recommend it when there are better, less-buggy, easier-to-read rogue-like games with better quality of life features. First off, I absolutely HATE the fonts. I spent too much time double-checking the wording and numbers since there is no UNDO feature. If you click on something and later realize it wasn't what you thought it was.... too bad... learn to read 'PixelatedBlobs.font'. Also, there are some tooltips, but when tiles have a dice on them, you can't see what the special tile is. This is compounded if the dice are locked to a tile and the tile suddenly becomes 'special'... it isn't always obvious. The game has potions but I completed all of the character runs and the final boss with Mango and barely used any potions... opting to increase my dice numbers, use growth/poison/lock and kill elites for more artifacts instead. At $15USD I got my monies worth with a few nights of playtime but I don't see myself continuing for the sake of achievements. If the devs included a standard (easier to read) font and perhaps an undo feature (until players learn the mechanics) as well as more tooltips (especially when dice are on the tiles) I might consider changing this to a 'recommends'... but there really are better card/dice roguelikes that have worked harder to earn you time and money.

I've been following this game for the last 2-3 years and I am very happy with this full release, it has lots of content and a fun battle system. I don't usually play roguelikes but this game is very fun.

Especially if this is on sale, I would grab it. I'm not sure on the staying power, this may be more of a 20hr game than a 40+hr game, but I do quite like it. Surely, it's worth the money. The music is especially good, except for that one chef-style boss, and the game is complex in a very fun way. I will say, push past the opener, I don't really like the first character. Both the poison and the parry character are way more fun, and genuinely seem far easier to win with. Just focus on the special events until you rescue the poison character and you'll be good. I do keep unlocking stuff at a steady pace, so maybe the influx of new items and relics or whatever the power-ups are called will keep runs feeling fresh. Overall, it's the same kind of game I like, done in a new way, with great art and music and multiple winning strategies, so I'm happy with my purchase and if you like games like this, I think you will be too, especially given the price. I actually have the music from the second area in my head right now... it's a banger. There's also a lot of really interesting special events, with great flavor text and unique rewards, I'm impressed with the breadth of the content here even if the actual enemies/bosses aren't super varied after a few play-throughs. I will say though, if you get the curse special event, don't keep cursing yourself... there's no reward for taking all the curses as I thought there may be, I just lost the run cus I was super cursed loooool
